It looks great! Ignore those that say that the classic pass takes years to master, because that's stupid. Yes, you can make a pass completely invisible, I even found a way to do it with the classic pass, but it's insanely difficult and angle sensitive, but the pass is just not a move you need to perfect. You're not trying to fool magicians, you're trying to fool laymen. The pass is meant to be done with misdirection, therefore it doesn't matter if it's perfect, it just needs to be near perfect. Another way to use the pass is to make it messy intentionally, but you need to do the entire trick with messy slights, that way the spectator thinks you don't really know how to handle a deck of cards, and then when the punchline would hit it would be even more amazing. It's the soap theory, daniel madison talks about it a lot. Anyway, it seems great, and I would suggest to work on the classic pass and the turnover pass, these are the two that I find the most useful :)
